description:
365 tiles at 16x16 for a city street at night, in the rain: wet asphalt, a sidewalk standing on a kerb, a polished plaza and standing water on all three. Three neon signs flicker on their posts and a hologram turns over the plaza, and their light lies on the road in pink, cyan and amber and mirrors in the puddles. Commercial use permitted, in unlimited projects, with no attribution required; the one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the pack itself.

Importers for RPG Maker MZ, Tiled and Godot ship in the download, and each was run by the engine it targets and made to count what it built.

What is in the download

  • 235 of the 365 tiles are transitions, 64% of the pack. 5 complete 47-mask autotile sets: every inner corner, outer corner, edge, junction and single. Completeness is checked mechanically on every build, because a set missing three tiles is broken in your map.
  • A sidewalk you paint as a mass. The sidewalk set is faced: where the road lies to the south it drops on a 3-pixel kerb with a lit lip, so bulb-outs, corners and crossings draw themselves. The kerb is a step, not a wall: tiles.json declares every ground tile walkable, the kerb face included.
  • Standing water on every surface. Three puddle sets put water on the road, the sidewalk and the plaza, and a plaza set sets the polished paving into the sidewalk.
  • The light is placed, not painted into the ground. Each sign has a matching 3x2 light pool for the road beside it and a 1x2 reflection for a puddle, in its own colour, so the road stays calm where there is no sign and glows where there is one.
  • 4 materials × 4 variants on a value ladder laid out before any art existed, so a night street does not collapse into one dark grey. The smallest gap on the ladder is 16.3 luma, measured from the shipped pixels rather than declared.
  • 24 objects across 50 prop tiles plus the animation frames: a street lamp, a bollard, a fire hydrant, a traffic cone, a bench, a palm in a planter, a vending machine, a noodle cart under a striped awning, a dumpster, bin bags and crates; a manhole, a drain grate and a zebra crossing for the road; three light pools and three reflections. Each ships transparent, and grounded on its floor with the contact shadow drawn.
  • 4 animated objects, 64 frames: a cocktail glass, an arrow and a star, each with a border tube chasing round the plate while the sign shimmers, half its tubes fail, it goes out and comes back dim; and a hologram turning over its projector. No two frames of a set are the same picture.
  • A finished 40x28 sample map with 170 objects on it and every autotile set placed, as a PNG, as JSON naming every cell by tile id, and as a .tmx that opens in Tiled.
  • 16 4x4 proof renders, one per repeating tile, so you can look for the grid line yourself.
  • Every tile as a loose PNG and as packed sheets: 431 files in total, and a tiles.json giving every tile's role, material, sheet slot, footprint and passability.

Three things to know before you buy

⚠️ This is a street, not a whole city. There are no building walls, facades or roofs in it: the pack is the ground a street is built on and the things that stand on it. At 365 tiles it is also a smaller pack than most of the series, and it is priced for that.

⚠️ The animation plays in Tiled and Godot, not in RPG Maker MZ. MZ animates tiles only through its A1 page, which holds animated water autotiles; this pack has none, so in MZ the signs and the hologram arrive as static frames on page C.

⚠️ The light pools and reflections are objects you place. They are not baked into the road, so a sign with no pool beside it casts no light until you put one there.

The importers were actually run

  • RPG Maker MZ: an A2 autotile sheet (the page MZ's own autotile brush paints) plus B/C object pages and a slot map. It composes correctly against MZ's own FLOOR_AUTOTILE_TABLE: 5 of 5 sets, 235 of 235 masked tiles, and 240 of 240 shapes came back byte-identical. The object pages carry every fill, every object and every animation frame.
  • Tiled: one .tsx per group, all 9 opened and rendered by Tiled 1.12.2's own tmxrasterizer and compared pixel for pixel with the shipped sheets: 508 sheet cells, 0 differing. The sample map's .tmx renders 1,146,880 pixels identical to the shipped PNG.
  • Godot 4: a .tres TileSet, loaded and verified in Godot 4.7.2: 9 atlas sources, 365 of 365 declared tiles built, 90 of 90 multi-cell footprints exact. Every sheet is referenced by a relative filename, so the folder loads from wherever you put it in a project.

What is proven, and what is not

The grid is exact, the palette is locked to 70 colours, the alpha is strictly binary with no anti-aliasing, every tile carries a declared role, and every autotile set is complete: exact checks, run on every build.

Seamlessness is not on that list. Every tile's wrap boundary is measured against its own interior, and every 4x4 repetition is rendered and reviewed; grid, palette and autotile completeness are machine-proven. The renders ship with the pack so you can judge them yourself.

The autotile sets

  • puddle_on_wetasph
  • kerbslab_on_wetasph
  • puddle_on_kerbslab
  • plaza_on_kerbslab
  • puddle_on_plaza

It fits the rest of the series

The 16x16 Verdant packs are drawn at one cell size in one style, so this street sits beside the others and a map can run straight out of it into another pack.

  • Verdant 17 — Urban Decay — the buildings this street lacks: concrete blockwork with graffiti, boarded openings and derelict interiors, on cracked asphalt
  • Verdant 30 — Rail Terminus — the station at the end of the street: platforms, track and a concourse
  • Verdant 32 — Orbital Station — the sci-fi interior for a city that goes off-world

AI disclosure

Tagged as AI-assisted. Precisely: every tile is drawn by a procedural generator written for this series, and that generator's code was written with AI assistance. No diffusion model is anywhere in the tile pipeline. Every image on this page, the cover included, is composed from the pack's own tiles and sample map.
